skill.name: employment-contract-templates
skill.description: Create employment offer letters, employment agreements, and employee handbook policy sections using structured HR templates and legal review reminders.
skill.summary: Draft customizable employment documents with clear placeholders, compliance prompts, and legal review guidance.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, public reference links, and HR wording containing terms such as paid and avoid. No executable code, command execution instruction, data exfiltration intent, or prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown fences were flagged as possible Ruby or shell backtick execution.
remediation.suggestion: Label fenced examples as plain text or markdown and keep them clearly documentation-only.

remediation.issue: External resource links can trigger network risk indicators.

remediation.issue: The templates are legal-adjacent and may be reused without jurisdiction review.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the legal disclaimer and prompt users to consult qualified employment counsel before use.

content.value_statement: Employment documents need clear terms, correct structure, and review checkpoints. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft offer letters, agreements, and handbook sections from editable templates.
actual_capabilities: Drafts structured employment offer letters with role, compensation, benefits, contingencies, and acceptance sections.
Creates employment agreement templates covering duties, term, compensation, confidentiality, IP, termination, and acknowledgments.
Produces employee handbook policy sections for EEO, harassment, attendance, PTO, holidays, conduct, technology, and social media.
Adds placeholders for company, employee, jurisdiction, dates, compensation, benefits, and policy choices.
Highlights legal review needs for jurisdiction-specific terms such as at-will language, non-competes, and dispute clauses.
Supports standardized HR documentation for hiring, onboarding, and policy updates.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or replace review by qualified employment counsel.
It does not verify current federal, state, local, or international employment law.
It does not negotiate terms or decide whether a restrictive covenant is enforceable.
It does not generate signed documents or manage employee records.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Hire Offer Letter
use_cases.description: Create a clear offer letter with role details, pay, benefits, contingencies, at-will language, and acceptance fields.

use_cases.title: Standardize Employment Agreements
use_cases.description: Draft a repeatable agreement template with compensation, confidentiality, intellectual property, termination, and governing law sections.

use_cases.title: Update Handbook Policies
use_cases.description: Write practical handbook sections for workplace conduct, anti-harassment reporting, PTO, holidays, technology use, and social media.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Offer Letter
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single candidate offer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an offer letter for a [JOB TITLE] at [COMPANY]. Include start date, location, employment type, compensation, benefits, contingencies, at-will language, and signature fields.

prompt_templates.title: Customize an Employment Agreement
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a role-specific agreement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an employment agreement for a [ROLE] in [JURISDICTION]. Include duties, term, compensation, benefits, confidentiality, IP assignment, termination, governing law, and legal review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Handbook Policy Sections
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for internal HR policy documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft employee handbook sections for EEO, anti-harassment, work hours, PTO, sick leave, holidays, conduct, technology use, and social media for a [COMPANY SIZE] organization.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Jurisdiction Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft employment document for placeholder terms, jurisdiction-sensitive clauses, missing HR details, and sections that need counsel review. Return a prioritized checklist with revision suggestions.

output_examples.input: Draft an offer letter for a full-time marketing manager with salary, benefits, background check, and acceptance deadline.
output_examples.output: A formatted offer letter with position details, compensation, benefits, contingencies, at-will language, acceptance instructions, and signature blocks.

output_examples.input: Create an employment agreement for a software engineer with confidentiality and IP assignment sections.
output_examples.output: A structured agreement covering employment duties, compensation, benefits, confidentiality, work product ownership, prior inventions, termination, and acknowledgments.

output_examples.input: Write handbook policy sections for PTO, holidays, harassment reporting, and technology use.
output_examples.output: Employee handbook text with policy headings, employee obligations, reporting steps, benefit placeholders, and review notes for company-specific rules.

best_practices: Provide the jurisdiction, worker classification, role type, pay structure, and company policy choices before drafting.
Keep placeholders visible until HR, finance, and legal reviewers confirm each term.
Ask for a final checklist of jurisdiction-sensitive clauses before sending any document for signature.
anti_patterns: Do not use templates as final legal advice without employment counsel review.
Do not copy non-compete, arbitration, or termination clauses across jurisdictions without checking enforceability.
Do not omit at-will, classification, benefits eligibility, or contingency language when it applies.

faq.question: Can this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides drafting templates and review prompts. A qualified employment lawyer should review final documents.

faq.question: Which documents can it draft?
faq.answer: It can draft offer letters, employment agreements, employee handbook sections, confidentiality terms, and related HR policy language.

faq.question: Does it support jurisdiction-specific requirements?
faq.answer: It can add jurisdiction placeholders and review reminders, but it does not verify current local law.

faq.question: Can it help with non-compete clauses?
faq.answer: Yes, it can draft placeholder language and warnings. Enforceability must be checked by counsel for the relevant jurisdiction.

faq.question: Is it useful for employee handbooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes policy patterns for EEO, harassment, attendance, PTO, holidays, conduct, technology, and social media.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the company name, role, jurisdiction, worker classification, pay terms, benefits, policies, and any required contingencies.
